key_insight: Quotienting out function-preserving channel scaling and permutations yields covering-number bounds with a sharp exponent S−H rather than S and a factorial divisor G.
engineering_relevance: Symmetry-aware capacity measures can sharpen statistical risk guarantees and help explain weight rebalancing and flat optimization directions.
method: Characterize quasianalytic function-preserving parameter maps as compositions of positive channel scaling and permutation.
Derive symmetry-reduced covering bounds for fully connected, convolutional, and residual ReLU/Leaky ReLU networks.
Prove matching lower bounds and extend the analysis to general continuous piecewise-linear activations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical proofs rather than empirical benchmarks: the exponent S−H is sharp in general, while the divisor G is attained for one-hidden-layer and generically identifiable networks.
watch_item: The symmetry characterization assumes quasianalytic parameter maps, and tightness of the permutation divisor is established only for specified network classes.
paper_title: Sharp Covering-Number Bounds for Feedforward ReLU Networks via Parameter Symmetries
